sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number for HR and payroll integrations; email: unique lookup for login and identity resolution; manager_id: team-level queries — find all direct reports of a manager; employment_status: filtering active/inactive/terminated employees for leave eligibility checks; department: department-scoped leave calendars and reports

table leave_types | fields: id, code, label, description, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: code: unique lookup by leave type code (annual, sick, emergency, etc.) for policy assignment and request validation; is_active: filtering active leave types when presenting options to employees

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type_id, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: leave_type_id: join with leave_types when resolving policy for a given leave type; is_active: filtering active policies during leave request validation and balance calculation

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: list all leave requests for a given employee (self-service dashboard); status: filter by status (pending approvals queue for managers, approved/rejected lists); leave_type_id: filter requests by leave type for reporting and balance reconciliation; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: find all requests approved by a specific manager for audit and manager dashboards; employee_id + status: composite access pattern — employee's requests filtered by status

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: look up balances for a specific employee (self-service dashboard); policy_id: join with leave_policies for entitlement rules and recalculation; fiscal_year: filter balances by fiscal year for annual reset and accrual jobs; employee_id + fiscal_year: composite access pattern — employee's balances scoped to a fiscal year; employee_id + policy_id + fiscal_year: unique constraint enforcement — one balance row per employee per policy per fiscal year

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type + entity_id: look up all audit records for a specific entity (e.g., all changes to a leave request); performed_by: find all actions performed by a specific user for compliance reports; action: filter by action type (APPROVE, REJECT, CREATE, etc.) for audit reports; performed_at: time-range queries for audit log browsing and retention policies

data_notes: Persistence slice for the leave management module. Six conceptual tables defined: employees (self-referencing manager FK), leave_types (lookup), leave_policies (linked to leave_types), leave_requests (core entity with FKs to employees and leave_types, plus self-referencing approved_by FK), leave_balances (per employee per policy per fiscal year), and audit_logs (GP-002 compliance). Six repository interfaces, each with a concrete Pg*Repository backed by PostgreSQL via the existing pg Pool connection at src/shared/db/connection.ts. All index rationales reflect the access patterns described in the feature: employee self-service dashboards, manager approval queues, calendar overlap detection, balance lookups, and audit reporting.
